text:
Vince Dunn plays nearly 23 minutes a night for Seattle, and too many of those minutes are spent in his own end. At five on five the Kraken get only 43% of the expected goals with him on the ice, three points worse than without him. Evolving-Hockey had him 125th among defensemen in wins above replacement last season, below where a top-pair defenseman should sit.

Context matters. Seattle as a team loses the chance battle most nights, and his partners have not been driving play. His own offense is steady: four goals on 3.3 expected and 12 points in 21 games, five on the power play, with a goal from the point against Anaheim this week. He blocks shots (31), and he played on the 2019 Blues team that won the Cup. Our range projects 36 to 55 points, about where he usually lands. The question for Seattle isn't whether Dunn can produce; it's whether he can help them spend less time defending.
